item.title: BIFL Index
item.description:
BIFL: Buy It for Life #

Below is a collection of the “best tools for the job” that I have researched so far.

I live by the philosophy of buying well, not often. Growing up, my family would re-buy the same shitty space heater and it would break every year. This not only creates waste on our precious planet, but it’s also more expensive in the long run!

Of course, living this philosophy requires some money, as the better quality item isn’t as cheap. But, if you save up and prioritize your funds, you can do it. You can also look into buying items used (e.g. eBay, FB marketplace/Craigslist). Often used items are in great condition, you can get a better deal, and keep an item out of the landfill.

item.title: foraging starter kit
item.description:
foraging starter kit #

so you want to eat stuff outside? #

by Matte Kirwin

last edited 28 July 2025

(sept 2022) i’m on vacation right now so this doc is incomplete. but it should have the bare minimum to get you started!

@eatingstuffoutside

getting inspired and learning #

Videos: #

  • Black Forager on TikTok and instagram is a great starting point.
    • she’s incredibly informative, inspiring, and funny

Books, general foraging #

  • Northeast Foraging, if you live in the northeast of the US this book is the perfect starter book. you can read over what’s available in your area and then start looking for it.
    • this was my first foraging book and i ate tons of stuff around boston using this book
  • there are books from the same series for other regions, e.g. midwest foraging.

Books, mushrooms #

  • Mushrooming without Fear
    • extreme beginner book, makes sure every shroom is from a completely non toxic family. so it’s impossible to get poisonous mushrooms if you’re following everything in the book
  • Mushrooming with Confidence
    • book by the same author. i think of this as the intermediate book that you’d read after mushrooming without fear.

identification #

🌿

Foraging Tip

**Golden Rule**: Always have 3 forms of positive ID before eating anything!
  • always have 3 forms of positive ID.
  • even then, taste test. only eat a little (tbh see if you have a bad digestive reaction). look up if it needs to be cooked first.

Safety First!

⚠️
Even with proper identification, start with small amounts to test for allergic reactions. Some edible plants require cooking to be safe!

the three forms of identification i use #

  • foraging books
  • Seek app by iNaturalist or Google Lens, these are helpful but not 100% reliable. ALWAYS check another form of ID.
  • facebook foraging groups, local to you (literally search on FB: foraging <location> or foraging and identification <location>
    • For Massachusetts people:
      • Foraging Southern New England
      • Foraging with Friends RI/MA/CT
      • The New England Mushroom Identification Forum
  • google “green leaves with white undersides massachusetts”
  • google whatever you think you have found thru apps or books and TRIPLE CHECK ALL IDENTIFYING CHARACTERISTICS ARE THE SAME

if you’re unsure at all DO NOT EAT

item.title: sourdough
item.description:
sourdough starter kit #

sourdough recipe #

Active mixing and kneading takes like 2-3 hours. It can be left in the fridge overnight, or left out at room temperature until the dough has risen.

  1. Mix everything in one bowl

    • 300g water
    • 10g salt
    • 100g active starter (eh it’s fine if it’s not totally active, as long as it’s been fed recently and there’s been enough time for the bacteria to populate all the substrate)
    • 450 bread flour
    • Mix everything until there’s no dry flour left

  2. Bulk fermentation / 1st rise
